questions.q: A customer says their new phone stopped working on day two. Which reply shows empathy?
options: Many phones stop working, so this is quite normal.
I understand that's hard. Let me help you fix it.
Please first tell me whether you dropped it anywhere.
You should have checked it in the shop itself.

questions.q: A chat customer writes everything in CAPITAL letters. What does it usually show?
options: They like big letters
There is a fault in the chat tool
They are a VIP customer
They are upset or in a hurry

questions.q: The line is noisy and you can't hear the customer well. What do you say?
options: Sorry, the line isn't clear. Could you repeat that, please?
I'll just note what I think you said.
Please call back from another number at once.
Let me end this call, it is too noisy.

questions.q: In a live chat, when should the first reply go to the customer?
options: After about 15 minutes
Within a minute or two
Only after you have the full answer
At the end of your shift

questions.q: Why do you write short notes on every call or ticket?
options: To make the call last longer
So the next agent knows what happened
Notes are only for managers to read
To fill the system with text

questions.q: An older customer finds the app hard to use. What is best?
options: Send a help link and end the call
Guide them slowly, step by step
Tell them to visit a store instead
Speak faster so the call is short

questions.q: A customer says ₹1,499 was debited by UPI, but the order shows 'failed'. What do you do first?
options: Ask them to pay again so the order goes through
Tell them the bank is at fault and to call it
Take the UPI reference number and check the payment
Cancel the order and close the ticket

questions.q: You need two minutes to check something in chat. Which message is best?
options: Please don't type anything until I come back to you.
I am checking. Please wait as long as it takes.
One sec, will see.
Thanks for waiting. I'm checking and will reply in 2 minutes.

questions.q: A customer demands a manager at once. The issue is simple and you can fix it. What is best?
options: Offer to fix it now; arrange the manager if they still want
Transfer to the manager without trying anything
Say managers don't take calls and refuse
Put them on hold for a long time so they calm down

questions.q: Which phrase should you avoid with an upset customer?
options: "I'm sorry for the trouble."
"Let me look into it."
"Thank you for telling us."
"Calm down."

questions.q: In an email reply to a customer, what should the first lines do?
options: Explain the history of the company
Give the update or answer they asked for
List every policy of the company
Ask them to phone the helpline

questions.q: A customer got the wrong item. The return pickup has failed twice and they are upset. What is the best next step?
options: Book a third pickup and tell them nothing more
Ask them to courier it back at their own cost
Apologise, raise it as priority with logistics, give a date and follow up
Close the ticket as 'customer not available'

questions.q: When should you escalate a complaint even if you could reply yourself?
options: When it mentions a legal notice or a safety risk
When the customer asks for the delivery date
When the call goes past five minutes
When the customer is very polite

questions.q: Your CSAT is high but repeat calls are rising. What does this most likely show?
options: Customers like you, but issues aren't fully solved
The CSAT survey tool is broken
The team has too many agents
Calls should be made shorter

questions.q: A customer starts crying while saying a hospital payment has failed. What do you do?
options: Ask them to stop crying so you can work
Transfer the call at once to another team
Speak gently, give a moment, then check the payment fast
Read out the refund policy word by word

questions.q: A customer posts an angry public review about you on social media. What is the right reply?
options: A long public reply proving the customer wrong
Ask them to delete the post before you help
A short public apology, then take details to private chat
Ignore it, as replying makes it worse

questions.q: A caller asks for the order details on their brother's account. They aren't the account holder. What do you do?
options: Share details only with the verified account holder
Share them, since they are family
Share only the delivery address
Ask for the brother's name and then share

questions.q: You must tell a customer the refund will take 7 more days. How do you say it?
options: Don't mention it unless they ask
Say it will 'maybe come tomorrow'
Say the bank is slow and you can't help
Say it clearly with the reason, the date and your next step

questions.q: A fix you gave yesterday didn't work and the customer calls back. What do you do first?
options: Repeat the same steps again more slowly
Say they must have done the steps wrong
Read the notes, own it, then try another fix or escalate
Open a fresh ticket and start from zero

questions.q: A customer is angry about a ₹299 monthly charge. You see they signed up for it themselves. How do you reply?
options: Tell them clearly that they are wrong
Refund it at once to avoid an argument
End the chat, since it is their mistake
Show the details kindly, without blame, and offer to cancel

task.title: Handle a caller whose refund is late
task.brief: Speak your answer out loud for 60–90 seconds, as if you are on the call. Situation: Ms. Kavya Reddy calls for the third time. She returned a pair of shoes worth ₹2,499. She was told the refund would come in 5–7 days. It is now day 12. You check and see the refund was approved but stuck at the bank step. A good answer: greets her and says your name, says sorry and shows you understand, tells her clearly what you found, says what you will do now and by when (with a ticket number), and closes politely. Speak calmly and clearly. Don't blame anyone and don't promise what you can't control.
key_points: Apologises and acknowledges this is the third call
Explains the refund is approved but stuck at the bank step
Gives a clear next step and a date or time
Gives a ticket or reference number
Does not blame the customer or the bank
Closes by asking if anything else is needed

rubric.label: Greeting and structure
rubric.guide: 0 = no greeting or order, 3 = greets but jumps around, 5 = greets, explains, gives next steps and closes in a clear order

rubric.label: Correct information
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong or made-up facts, 3 = mostly right but vague on next steps, 5 = accurate status, clear action, date and reference

rubric.label: Empathy
rubric.guide: 0 = cold or blaming, 3 = says sorry once, 5 = sincere apology, notes the repeat calls and stays calm and kind

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable with some confusion, 5 = short, simple sentences the customer can easily follow
